title: [BUG] Frequent test TIMEOUTs in 7.2, 7.4 and 8.0
body: I am experiencing frequent test TIMEOUTs in Redis 7.2, 7.4 and 8.0 in the Gentoo test environment. I noticed them after the 7.2.10, 7.4.5 and 8.0.3 security releases, although older 7.2.9, 7.4.4 and 8.0.2 builds are now affected too. The logs time out during active-defrag tests such as “Active defrag big keys” and then kill still-running Redis servers.

symptoms_visible: My Gentoo test runs for Redis 7.2, 7.4 and 8.0 frequently end with TIMEOUT while an Active defrag big keys test is in progress, followed by still-running Redis servers being killed.
N0.label: N0 cross-version Gentoo test timeouts reported

symptoms_visible: The timeout reproduces when I run the Redis ebuild test in an updated Gentoo testing container.
Changing among OpenSSL 3.3.3, 3.4.1, 3.4.2, 3.5.0 and 3.5.1 does not change the timeout.
N1.label: N1 Gentoo reproduction detailed

symptoms_visible: The same test passes in my virtual machine with kernel 6.11.4 but times out with kernel 6.15.2; kernels 6.12 and 6.13 also pass.
The test passes again with the 6.16 release candidates.
N2.label: N2 kernel-dependent range measured

symptoms_visible: With net.ipv4.tcp_rmem increased to 18 MB or more, my Redis tests stop timing out.
N3.label: N3 TCP receive-buffer probe succeeds

symptoms_visible: After I backport the candidate patch to 8.0.3, the active-defrag test list looks complete through Active defrag big list, but the run still ends with TIMEOUT and kills still-running Redis servers.
Active defrag big keys is no longer the test left in progress, but the timeout after Active defrag big list remains.
N4_x.label: N4_x candidate patch leaves a residual timeout

symptoms_visible: After running the tests with the merged changes, the active-defrag timeout no longer occurs; it seems fixed.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter verifies merged fix

question_patterns: Can you share the detailed steps you use to reproduce the timeout in the Gentoo environment?
Are you running the tests directly on Gentoo, and what commands reproduce the failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I have a Docker container with updated ~amd64 Gentoo. I install the dependencies with `emerge -qav1ok --with-test-deps --with-bdeps=y dev-db/redis`, then run `ebuild /var/db/repos/gentoo/dev-db/redis/redis-8.0.3.ebuild clean test`. I also downgraded the container to its Redis 8.0.2-era state and it still timed out.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I cannot reproduce it with the normal Redis test suite; it occurs only in an unrelated downstream integration test.
The same commands reproduce it on a Gentoo virtual machine rather than in Docker.

question_patterns: What differs between the environment where this previously passed and the environment where it now times out?
Did the host kernel or container configuration change?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The only difference I can see is the host kernel. It was originally 6.11.4 and is now 6.15.2.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c2, reporter's Gentoo system: participant1 requested exact reproduction steps. The reporter supplied the container and ebuild commands, noted the host-kernel change, and separately volunteered that several OpenSSL versions all reproduce the timeout.

question_patterns: Can you compare the same test under the old and new kernels to see whether the kernel version controls the result?
Could you reproduce this in otherwise identical virtual machines using the two kernel versions?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created a virtual machine and ran the same test. It passes with kernel 6.11.4 and times out with 6.15.2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same test times out under both 6.11.4 and 6.15.2.
It passes on 6.11.5 and times out on 6.15.2, with the rest of the setup unchanged.

question_patterns: Which intermediate kernel versions pass or time out?
Can you bisect the kernel range and paste the first bad commit reported by the run?
What raw result does the kernel bisection produce?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My kernel bisection reports `8c670bdfa58e48abad1d5b6ca1ee843ca91f7303` as the first bad commit. It is included in Linux 6.14.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection reports a Redis source change rather than any Linux kernel commit.

question_patterns: Does the same test still time out on a current release-candidate kernel?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the 6.16 release candidates and the test passed without timeouts.

question_patterns: Can you bisect between the failing kernel and the release candidate and paste the first commit where the test passes again?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The reverse bisection reports `572be9bf9d0d96242dd7977ce456009b6c690dce` as the commit where it starts working again. It changes a buffer size, although I do not know why that affects the test.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same first-good commit is reported from a different pair of kernel tags.

edges.comment: Thread c3-c10, reporter's VM and kernel builds: after participant1 asked for more clues, the reporter compared kernels and performed both kernel bisections. The answers retain the raw pass/timeout observations and commit outputs; the socket-buffer interpretation was supplied later by participant1 and is not placed in the reporter's answers.

question_patterns: Could you increase net.ipv4.tcp_rmem locally and report whether the test still times out?
Please try several larger values for net.ipv4.tcp_rmem and tell me at what point the timeout changes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The tests stop timing out if I increase `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` to 18 MB or more.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The tests still time out with net.ipv4.tcp_rmem increased well beyond 18 MB.
They stop timing out at 20 MB rather than exactly 18 MB.
The test output uses a different temporary socket name on each run.

edges.comment: Thread c10-c13, reporter's Gentoo test environment: participant1 hypothesized TCP buffer exhaustion because the test sends many commands without reading replies, then explicitly requested an rmem probe. The reporter supplied only the observed threshold.

solution.intent: Backport and test the linked candidate Redis patch intended to address the active-defrag test timeout.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the linked candidate patch to the affected 8.0.3 tree and rerun the full test suite under the same failing kernel.

edges.comment: Thread c14-c17, reporter's backported Redis 8.0.3 tree: participant1 asked the reporter to test the linked candidate PR. It addressed the earlier Active defrag big keys hang, but the run still timed out after Active defrag big list, so the candidate alone was not a complete resolution.

solution.intent: Complete and merge the Redis test fix for both active-defrag timeout cases, accounting for the TCP receive-buffer pressure exposed by newer kernels, then require the reporter to verify the current code in the original Gentoo environment.
solution.concrete_example: Do not stop at the candidate that only clears the Active defrag big keys hang. Complete the test-side fix so the remaining Active defrag big list run also finishes when TCP buffering is constrained, merge it, and ask the reporter to run the current code in the same Gentoo environment and report what happens.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied kernel pass/fail ranges, raw bisection commit outputs, the 18 MB tcp_rmem threshold, and the residual timeout after Active defrag big list. Participant1 connected those measurements to the test sending many commands without consuming replies, allowing TCP receive-buffer pressure to stall the test. That causal interpretation is engineer-side inference rather than a fact the reporter independently diagnosed.

edges.comment: Thread c16-c20, reporter's original affected environment: participant1 recognized that the first candidate handled Active defrag big keys but not Active defrag big list, later reported that the complete fix had merged, and requested verification. The terminal-side observation records the reporter's subsequent confirmation that it seemed fixed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as TCP receive-buffer pressure during active-defrag tests that send many commands without consuming the replies, allowing the test to stall on affected newer Linux kernels.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the kernel-dependent pass/timeout results, the kernel bisection outputs, and the observation that raising net.ipv4.tcp_rmem to at least 18 MB prevents the timeout.
Must not attribute the failure to the tested OpenSSL versions, since all of them reproduced the timeout.
Must not treat the first candidate patch as the complete fix: it cleared the earlier Active defrag big keys case but a timeout remained after Active defrag big list.
The complete Redis test fix must cover both the Active defrag big keys and Active defrag big list timeout cases.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the complete fix in the original Gentoo environment and must not declare resolution before that verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical distribution maintainer or package tester who can reproduce ebuild failures, manage Gentoo testing containers, compare kernel versions, bisect the Linux kernel, backport Redis patches, and modify sysctl values.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative, and evidence-driven; supplies exact commands, version ranges, commit outputs, and focused test results while clearly stating uncertainty about mechanisms.
